stories.title: Ghana addresses mental health treatment gap
stories.summary: More than 2.3 million people in Ghana live with mental health conditions, facing a 98 percent treatment gap. Local authorities in the Daffiama-Bussie-Issa District are now supplementing clinical care with livelihood support to help patients manage costs and social exclusion. Clinical care is being joined by community support.

stories.title: Kerala renames mental health centres
stories.summary: The Kerala government will rename its mental health centres as Regional Institutes for Happiness and Wellness. The decision follows objections from the Indian Medical Association and the Indian Psychiatric Society regarding the previous name. The state government submitted the change to the high court on Tuesday.

stories.title: Mental health summit returns to Mumbai
stories.summary: The Independent Mental Health Summit returns for its fourth edition this November. The event is billed as India’s largest independent gathering focused on the sector. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: North Carolina advocates seek mental health funding
stories.summary: North Carolina needs four times its current number of school social workers and psychologists to meet national recommendations. The Child Fatality Task Force is pushing for increased financial resources in the upcoming legislative session. The state has recorded recent improvements in youth mental health, according to officials.

stories.title: Texas Health Resources receives suicide prevention grant
stories.summary: The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration awarded Texas Health Resources a grant of up to 1.5 million dollars. The funds will support the implementation of Zero Suicide tactics across north Texas hospitals. The organization was one of 32 applicants selected from a pool of 235.

stories.title: University of Idaho expands pediatric mental health access
stories.summary: The University of Idaho received 1.2 million dollars to launch the Idaho Pediatric Psychiatry Access Line. The program aims to connect primary care providers with specialists to bypass wait times that currently reach 12 months. Idaho is reportedly the only state without such a service.

stories.title: Study examines digital mental health adoption
stories.summary: A study of Palestinian citizens of Israel found that 16.7 percent of surveyed adults use digital mental health platforms. Adoption was linked to higher education and positive attitudes toward the technology. These factors remained significant even when accounting for existing structural barriers to traditional in-person care.

stories.title: Review maps barriers to digital therapeutics
stories.summary: A systematic review in BMC Digital Health synthesizes barriers to the adoption of prescription digital therapeutics for mental health. The study examines perspectives from patients, providers, and administrators. It aims to clarify why usage remains limited despite the potential to address gaps in treatment access.

stories.title: Youth and caregiver reports on mental health differ
stories.summary: A study indicates that youth and caregivers frequently disagree on psychiatric diagnoses. Youth tend to report internal issues like depression, while caregivers focus on observable conduct problems. Researchers suggest that both perspectives are necessary for an accurate assessment of a child’s mental health.

stories.title: Global study tracks youth mental health decline
stories.summary: A study reports a global decline in youth mental health, citing a lack of emotional stability and resilience. The lead author describes the trend as a flashing red light. Meanwhile, the same demographic is increasingly turning to AI-based therapy as global instability continues.

stories.title: Wyoming community faces mental health concerns after layoffs
stories.summary: The elimination of 350 jobs at WE Soda in Sweetwater County has raised concerns regarding the mental health of displaced workers. Local observers note that while economic success is measured in tax revenue and job growth, the personal impact of industrial downsizing is rarely discussed.

stories.title: Nature walks linked to stress reduction
stories.summary: A study from North Carolina State University found that nature walks have a more restorative effect on stress levels than urban environments. Students reported feeling more refreshed after exposure to natural sights and sounds. The effects were described as immediately apparent by researchers.

stories.title: Mindfulness and biofeedback impact migraine pain
stories.summary: A systematic review found that mindfulness and biofeedback do not reduce the frequency of migraine attacks. However, the interventions demonstrated efficacy in lowering subjective pain intensity and improving quality of life. The findings were published in Frontiers in Neuroscience.

stories.title: Forbes explores awe and workplace wellness
stories.summary: A recent article suggests five practices to incorporate awe into the workday to improve wellness. The piece focuses on how small shifts in perspective can influence professional life. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Spiritual practitioners mark 11/11 portal
stories.summary: Spiritual practitioners and numerologists consider November 11 a powerful date for new beginnings. The 11/11 portal is frequently associated with manifestation and alignment. The date is viewed by some as an opportunity to call in blessings or make changes.

stories.title: Book explores gratitude through coffee
stories.summary: Writer AJ Jacobs explores the concept of gratitude by tracing the hundreds of people involved in producing a single cup of coffee. His book, Thanks a Thousand, documents the journey to thank everyone in the supply chain. Most people take the process for granted, according to Jacobs.

stories.title: Mindfulness linked to student sleep quality
stories.summary: A meta-analysis in Frontiers in Public Health suggests mindfulness interventions can improve sleep quality for university students. Researchers noted substantial statistical inconsistency across the ten trials reviewed. They urged cautious interpretation of the overall effect size regarding these non-pharmacological sleep aids.

stories.title: Exercise linked to adolescent well-being
stories.summary: A review of 23 studies involving 10,000 young people found that satisfying the need for personal competence links exercise to higher life satisfaction. The research evaluated Self-Determination Theory among youth aged ten to 18 years. Findings suggest exercise supports subjective vitality and psychological flourishing.

stories.title: Small lifestyle changes linked to heart health
stories.summary: A study of 53,242 adults in the European Journal of Preventive Cardiology suggests that 11 more minutes of sleep, 4.5 more minutes of exercise, and a quarter cup of vegetables daily are tied to 10 percent fewer major heart problems. Precision is now a dietary requirement.

stories.title: Sleep starts linked to anxiety
stories.summary: Research from Paris Lodron University Salzburg finds that frequent hypnic jerks are associated with poorer sleep quality and heightened anxiety. The study of 194 adults suggests these jolts are not just isolated twitches but manifest alongside sensory flashes and cognitive hyperarousal. The brain is apparently keeping its own hours.

stories.title: Survey Links Frequent Sleep Starts to Anxiety and Poorer Sleep Quality
stories.summary: A new survey examining transient sleep-onset phenomena reveals that frequent sleep starts are significantly linked to poorer sleep quality, stronger dysfunctional beliefs about rest, and heightened anxiety symptoms. stories.title: College students report cycle of poor sleep
stories.summary: A study published in Emerging Adulthood examines how college students struggle to prioritize rest despite competing life demands. Researchers Royette T. Dubar and Danielle Greene conclude that students often feel powerless to improve their sleep quality. The academic schedule remains indifferent to the circadian rhythm.

stories.title: Cycling Every Day vs. One Long Weekend Ride: Which Is Better for Losing Body Fat?
stories.summary: A 45-minute ride after work and a four-hour cycling session on Sunday can both contribute to weight loss, but they represent very different training schedules. For cyclists trying to reduce body fat, the question is whether riding more frequently produces better results than concentrating exercise

stories.title: Spin class heart rates may not reflect power
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of León found a disconnect between cardiovascular effort and mechanical power during indoor cycling. While heart rates reached 94 percent of maximum, average power output remained at 110 to 120 watts. The stationary bike is working harder than the rider.

stories.title: Faith meets fitness in Keralam
stories.summary: St. Joseph’s Church in Kuriachira has opened a gym on its premises to encourage parishioners to stretch and sweat. The facility, which has no fixed hours, is frequented by altar boys and senior citizens alike. The church describes the initiative as a healthy new dimension to life.

stories.title: Review suggests less protein may aid longevity
stories.summary: A review of over 350 studies published in Cell Press Blue suggests that restricting protein intake could slow biological ageing and improve metabolic health. The findings challenge the long-standing industry message that more protein is better. The sector is now being asked to reconsider its product development.

stories.title: Food quality may outweigh calorie counting for longevity
stories.summary: A review in The Innovation Nutrition argues that food quality, including fiber and fat types, may influence health as much as calorie restriction. While higher fiber intake was tied to lower death risk, the authors note these human studies show associations rather than proof of direct cause.

stories.title: Coffee consumption linked to gut physiology
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Copenhagen used swallowable electronic capsules to track the digestive tracts of coffee drinkers. The study found that regular consumption is associated with greater gut microorganism diversity and changes in intestinal acidity. The capsule measured transit time, temperature, pH levels and intestinal contractions.

stories.title: Danish study tracks coffee and gut health
stories.summary: A secondary analysis from the University of Copenhagen links regular coffee drinking to a more diverse gut microbiome and lower pH levels in the small intestine. Researchers used SmartPill capsules to track internal metrics, suggesting that caffeine metabolites may support digestion through increased colon contractions.

stories.title: Coffee drinkers show more diverse gut bacteria
stories.summary: A small Danish study of 61 adults found that regular coffee drinkers host a wider range of gut bacteria and have more acidic small intestines. While three bacterial groups appeared higher in frequent drinkers, the researchers noted these differences faded after statistical correction and results show only links.

stories.title: Japan study links diet to gut bacteria groups
stories.summary: A study of 6,803 people published in Nature Medicine identifies two opposing gut bacteria groups. One is associated with plant foods, fermented items, coffee and exercise, while the other links to refined carbohydrates and sugary drinks. The research was conducted by several Japanese medical and scientific institutions.

stories.title: Coffee study examines gut activity
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Copenhagen found that adults drinking one to five cups of coffee regularly had higher small intestine acidity and more colon contractions. The nine-day study tracked 60 adults. The authors state that further work is required to fully understand the observed digestive effects.

stories.title: Dietitian offers tips for post-festive eating
stories.summary: With festive treats still filling homes after Diwali, a senior dietitian suggests six ways to return to balanced eating. The advice focuses on mindful consumption rather than eliminating favorite foods entirely. The goal is to transition back to a regular routine without giving up everything you love.

stories.title: Doctors warn against longevity myths
stories.summary: The wellness economy is growing, with 800 longevity-focused clinics now operating in the United States. Doctors suggest that the most important factors for healthy ageing do not cost anything, despite the industry's focus on expensive wearables and supplements. The market for longevity tips is currently quite active.

stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Sultan Nazrin calls for inclusive ageing
stories.summary: The Sultan of Perak has stated that healthy ageing must not be a commodity reserved for the wealthy. He argued that the silver economy should represent a structural realignment toward social stability rather than just a marketing frontier. True inclusivity remains a goal for modern civilisation.

stories.title: Healthy ageing should be accessible to all
stories.summary: Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah of Perak stated that healthy ageing must be inclusive by design. He argued that society is judged by whether its opportunities reach vulnerable citizens. The Sultan described the development of accessible services and technologies as both good social policy and a moral obligation.

stories.title: Herbalife India and IISc launch ageing study
stories.summary: Herbalife India and the Indian Institute of Science have launched a multi-city study involving 1,000 participants. The initiative aims to evaluate the relationships between metabolic health, gut diversity and community participation. The research is conceptualized around the themes of health and happiness among Indian adults.

stories.title: Higher diet quality linked to lower obesity
stories.summary: Research published in Frontiers in Nutrition indicates that adults who maintain high diet quality scores experience lower rates of new-onset obesity. The study tracked non-obese participants over multiple survey waves to evaluate the relationship between nutritional quality and weight gain in the Chinese population.

stories.title: Fruit fly study challenges longevity theory
stories.summary: Researchers investigating the sex gap in longevity examined 277 strains across three fruit fly species. The study challenges the toxic Y chromosome hypothesis, which suggests that repetitive elements on the Y chromosome drive shorter lifespans in males. The team sought to identify the evolutionary forces behind the gap.

stories.title: Obesity linked to lower death risk in dementia
stories.summary: A study of 4,500 older adults found that those who were overweight or obese at the time of a dementia diagnosis had a 16% to 27% lower risk of death. Researchers suspect extra energy reserves may help patients survive, though the reason for the survival advantage remains unclear.

stories.title: Study finds most obese people may be healthy
stories.summary: A University College London study of 7,000 people suggests 69 percent of those classified as obese by BMI are not at risk when other factors are considered. Researchers argue that definitions of obesity should include fat distribution and organ function. Being heavy is now a matter of perspective.

stories.title: Vice-President inaugurates Ayurvedic paediatric conference
stories.summary: The Vice-President of India inaugurated KAUMARACON-2026 at the All India Institute of Ayurveda in New Delhi. The event marks the third international conference on Ayurvedic paediatrics and celebrates the Institute’s decade of progress in education and research. The government continues to seek scientific validation for traditional systems.

stories.title: Greenspace Herbs aims to bridge tradition and research
stories.summary: Greenspace Herbs is working to align traditional Ayurvedic knowledge with modern research standards. Founder Shafiulla Hirehal Nuruddin, an industrial engineer by training, is focusing the company on scientific validation and transparency in the herbal extracts industry. The company is currently seeking to modernise traditional wellness practices.

stories.title: Cura launches herbal juice range
stories.summary: Wellness brand Cura has released a line of herbal juices, including formulations for gut and liver health. The products feature a 48-hour brewing process and detailed ingredient transparency on packaging. The company is relying on 27 years of history to support its new range of bottled wellness.

stories.title: Aarogyavind Wellness announces new premium brand
stories.summary: Aarogyavind Wellness Private Limited is preparing to launch a premium range of Ayurvedic and herbal products. The company aims to redefine the wellness sector by focusing on purity and high-quality presentation for modern consumers. It promises to bridge the gap between traditional practices and contemporary health needs.

stories.title: Greenspace Herbs launches intimate wellness product
stories.summary: Greenspace Herbs has launched Spatikama, a botanical nutraceutical for women, at SupplySide Global. The formulation combines licorice, fenugreek, and ginger extract. While the ingredients have a long history of use in Indian households, the product is being marketed under the tagline Bloom Her Desire.

stories.title: Jeena Sikho incorporates genomics subsidiary
stories.summary: Jeena Sikho Lifecare has incorporated Ayugenomics Private Limited to integrate genomics with Ayurvedic research and diagnostics. The parent company holds a 60 percent stake in the new entity, which was established with an acquisition cost of 300,000 rupees. The subsidiary aims to combine omics sciences with AYUSH systems.

stories.title: Ayurvedic herbal extract market continues to grow
stories.summary: The market for Ayurvedic herbal extracts is experiencing significant growth, driven by a combination of traditional use and modern acceptance. Market size is expected to rise from 52.05 billion dollars as global interest in plant-based therapies expands. The industry remains positioned for continued upward momentum.

stories.title: Ayurvedic tips for winter wellness
stories.summary: Ayurvedic guidance suggests that winter nutrition should be tailored by age. Recommendations include balanced meals for children, whole grains for working adults, and easy-to-digest, fresh food for senior citizens. The advice focuses on seasonal vegetables and protein sources to support immunity during the colder months.

stories.title: Go Greek Yogurt highlights ancient traditions
stories.summary: Go Greek Yogurt creator Tanja Murgel-Subotic suggests that the foundations of wellness are already part of human nature. She views the body as an intelligent system capable of repair, though she notes these biological capacities have limits and do not replace professional medical care.
